notes: Single-file fix with a regression test. The fix is exactly the EXIF-orientation handling the issue describes — no extras.
input:
## Issue summary

Image converter rotates EXIF-orientation-6 JPEGs incorrectly. Pictures shot in portrait on iPhone come out 90° clockwise rotated when extracted via the converter, even though they display correctly in macOS Preview.

## Files touched

```
src/converters/image_converter.py
tests/test_image_converter.py
```

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/converters/image_converter.py b/src/converters/image_converter.py
--- a/src/converters/image_converter.py
+++ b/src/converters/image_converter.py
@@ -67,6 +67,11 @@ class ImageConverter:
     def _open(self, path):
         img = Image.open(path)
+        # PIL ignores EXIF orientation by default; apply it before
+        # downstream OCR + thumbnail steps so we don't hand them a
+        # rotated buffer.
+        from PIL import ImageOps
+        img = ImageOps.exif_transpose(img)
         return img

diff --git a/tests/test_image_converter.py b/tests/test_image_converter.py
--- a/tests/test_image_converter.py
+++ b/tests/test_image_converter.py
@@ -34,3 +34,11 @@ def test_basic_jpeg():
+
+def test_exif_orientation_6_normalized():
+    """iPhone portrait — EXIF tag 6 = rotate 90 CW for display."""
+    converter = ImageConverter()
+    img = converter.open_image('tests/fixtures/portrait_o6.jpg')
+    # Source is 4032x3024; with orientation applied → 3024x4032
+    assert img.width == 3024 and img.height == 4032
```
